title: syntaxdiagram-d

syntaxdiagram-d

title: <delim>
content:
<delim>

The <delim> element represents delimiter characters that appear in syntax notation. It belongs to the syntax diagram domain and is used to mark punctuation or separator characters as part of a command or language syntax expression.

Source: dita-lang technical content language reference.

title: <fragment>
content:
<fragment>

The <fragment> element contains a named fragment of syntax that can be defined once and then referenced elsewhere in a syntax diagram. It is part of the syntax diagram domain and helps authors model reusable subexpressions inside command or grammar notation.

Source: dita-lang technical content language reference.

title: <fragref>
content:
<fragref>

The <fragref> element references a syntax fragment defined elsewhere with <fragment>. It is used inside syntax diagrams when a reusable fragment needs to be included by reference instead of rewritten inline.

Source: dita-lang technical content language reference.

title: <groupchoice>

<groupchoice>

title: <groupcomp>
content:
<groupcomp>

<groupseq>

title: <kwd>
content:
<kwd>

The <kwd> element marks a keyword or literal token in syntax notation. It is a core syntax diagram domain element used when documenting command names, literal options, or reserved words in a formal syntax pattern.

title: <oper>

<oper>

title: <repsep>
content:
<repsep>

The <repsep> element marks the separator used between repeated syntax items. It is part of the syntax diagram domain and is useful when documenting lists or repeated arguments that use a visible separator in the syntax.

title: <synph>
content:
<synph>

The <synph> element represents a syntax phrase inside the DITA syntax diagram domain. It is used for inline syntax fragments and reusable syntax wording where phrase-level syntax markup is needed rather than a full block-level syntax diagram.

Source: dita-lang technical content language reference.

<synblk>

title: Arguments and options for the dita command
content:
Arguments and options for the dita command

The DITA Open Toolkit `dita` command requires the main file and output format for a normal transform, or a project file for multi-deliverable publishing. Core invocation forms: `dita --input=<file> --format=<transtype> [options]` and `dita --project=<file> [options]`. The short forms `-i file` and `-f name` correspond to the common parameters `args.input` and `transtype`. Input is usually a DITA map but may be a single topic; paths can be absolute, relative to `args.input.dir`, or relative to the current directory when `args.input.dir` is unset.

`--output=dir` / `-o dir` sets the output directory (`output.dir`); default is typically an `out` subdirectory. Pass arbitrary build parameters with GNU-style `--parameter=value` or Ant-style `-Dparameter=value`. Use `--propertyfile=file` for a `.properties` file; CLI values override the file. `--resource=file` / `-r file` supplies additional resource files (e.g. key map with a lone topic, or reltables map with a chapter map) and maps to `args.resources`.

`--filter=` accepts DITAVAL file paths; on Windows separate multiple paths with `;` inside quotes, on macOS/Linux use `:`, or pass `--filter=` multiple times (order matters; first wins on conflicts). `--temp=dir` / `-t dir` sets `dita.temp.dir`. For PDF, `--theme=file` applies a PDF theme configuration.

Subcommands (no transform): `dita plugins`, `dita transtypes`, `dita install`, `dita uninstall <id>`, `dita validate --input=...`, `dita version`, `dita deliverables <project>`, `dita init`, and help via `dita --help` or `dita <subcommand> --help`.

Logging and diagnostics: `--verbose` / `-v`, `--debug` / `-d`, `--logfile=file` / `-l`, optional `--logger=json`, `--stacktrace` (with verbose/debug), `--no-color` or `NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb`. Use `--repeat=N` to benchmark repeated runs.

title: Generating revision bars
content:
Generating revision bars

DITA Open Toolkit can generate revision bars (change bars) in PDF output when you flag revised content in a DITAVAL file using the `<revprop>` element. This page documents the PDF2 customization path for change bars, not general DITA authoring.

DITAVAL configuration
Use `<revprop action="flag" changebar="..." color="..."/>` inside your DITAVAL. When `@action` is `flag`, DITA-OT reads:
- `@changebar` — the line style for the revision bar. Values follow XSL-FO change-bar styles (for example `solid`, `groove`). Default: `groove`.
- `@color` — the bar color using any XSL-FO color value (named colors or hex). Default: `black`.

Example
```xml
<revprop action="flag" changebar="solid" color="green"/>
```

Runtime behavior
- DITA-OT places the bar near the edge of the text column with a default offset of 2 mm.
- Offset, placement, and width are not currently configurable through DITAVAL attributes.
- XSL-FO 1.1 supports rule-based change bars only; text-style revision indicators (for example numbers instead of rules) are not supported by the standard PDF transformation. Antenna House Formatter offers a proprietary extension, but the DITA-OT PDF transformation does not use it.

title: PDF themes
content:
PDF themes

DITA Open Toolkit 4.0 and later include the `com.elovirta.pdf` plug-in, which extends the default PDF2 transformation with a theme parameter. The `--theme` option takes a path to a theme file and changes PDF styling without editing XSLT stylesheets.

What themes control
Themes can adjust cover page images, page size and orientation, numbering, font properties, background colors and borders, spacing, and running content such as page headers and footers.

Command example
```
dita --project=samples/project-files/pdf.xml \
     --theme=path/to/custom-theme-file.yaml
```

Theme file structure
- **Page settings** — use `size` and `orientation`; margins via `top`, `outside`, `bottom`, and `inside`.
- **Header and footer** — `content` keys under `header` or `footer` accept static text or variable references in curly braces.
- **Styles** — block and inline presentation via `style` keys using XSL-FO definitions plus style-specific keys.
- **Variables** — previously defined keys can be referenced from other key values.
- **Extending themes** — a theme can inherit from another theme with the `extends` key.
- **Syntactic sugar** — shorthand keys are desugared to verbose equivalents before stylesheet generation.
- **Examples** — theme files may be JSON or YAML; sample themes live under `docsrc/samples/themes` in the DITA-OT installation.

title: Understanding the output presets
content:
Understanding the output presets in AEM Guides

Adobe Experience Manager Guides supports seven output preset types. An output preset defines how a DITA map is transformed and where the published output is delivered.

The seven preset types
1. AEM Sites — Publish structured content into Adobe Experience Manager Sites for web delivery and Sites workflows.
2. PDF — Generate PDF using the Native PDF engine with CSS/template-based styling.
3. Knowledge Base — Produce knowledge-base style HTML suited for support portals.
4. HTML5 — Standard HTML5 webhelp-style documentation output.
5. EPUB — E-book format for digital readers.
6. JSON — Structured JSON output for downstream applications or headless delivery.
7. Custom — DITA-OT or other custom transform pipelines configured by your organization.

When to use each
- AEM Sites: content must live in AEM for tagging, personalization, or Sites publishing.
- PDF / Native PDF: printable, regulated, or offline documentation.
- Knowledge Base: searchable support articles with KB navigation patterns.
- HTML5: classic static web documentation bundles (often SFTP or static hosting).
- EPUB: distribution to e-readers.
- JSON: programmatic consumption of structured content.
- Custom: legacy DITA-OT pdf2 FO pipelines, custom plugins, or bespoke output formats.

title: Content Reuse Report
content:
Content Reuse Report in AEM Guides

The Content Reuse Report helps project managers and business owners understand how much topic content is reused across a selected repository path. The report scans the chosen parent folder and all child folders, then calculates average content reuse as Content Reuse Instances divided by Total Topic Count.

Prerequisite
Post-processing workflows must be enabled for the report to work correctly. If the report does not calculate reuse, check with an administrator that post-processing workflows are enabled.

How users open it
Go to Adobe Experience Manager > Tools > Guides > Content Reuse Report. Select Browse to choose the folder where topics reside, or enter the path manually, then select Generate Report.

How the report works
The report counts first-level direct content references and topic references. Content Reuse Instances is the sum of the Number of Times Reused values. The most reused topic appears in the summary, and selecting that topic opens its preview.

Report sections
The Report Summary shows Average Content Reuse and the Most Reused Topic. The Details table includes Title, UUID, Size, Status, Number of Times Reused, and Referenced By.

Important calculation behavior
Number of Times Reused is calculated from the Referenced By entries minus one. Referenced By lists the direct first-level topics where the corresponding topic is referenced, with referenced file UUIDs shown in brackets. Selecting topic title links opens topic preview.

Export
Users can export the Content Reuse Report as CSV from the Export to CSV link.

title: Understanding session timeouts in Experience Manager Guides
content:
Understanding session timeouts in AEM Guides

AEM Guides signs users out after a configured period of inactivity. The idle timeout is configured in Adobe Experience Manager, not by individual authoring content. When the session expires, AEM Guides displays an alert and prevents further changes to the application, reducing the risk of editing against an invalid session.

How timeout detection works
AEM Guides sends a background request to token.json every 30 seconds to validate whether the session is still active. If the session is active, a valid token is returned. If inactivity has expired the session, an empty token is returned and the session is treated as inactive.

User experience after expiry
When an inactive session is detected, a pop-up tells the user they have been signed out and disables application interaction. Selecting OK refreshes the browser and redirects to login. After login, the user returns to the last opened AEM Guides page.

Authoring guidance
Users should save work regularly in the Editor, especially before stepping away for a long time.

title: DITA map report from the Map Console
content:
DITA map report from the Map Console

The Reports tab in Map Console lets users check map integrity and work with four report types for the current DITA map: Topic List, Metadata, Multimedia, and Broken links. Open a DITA map in Map view, select Open in map console, then select Reports from the left panel.

Topic List report
Shows topics in the map with fields such as title, file name, UUID, file location, reference type, document state, author, and parent map. Users can filter by reference type, document state, and author. Refresh updates the list after map or reference changes, and Download exports the selected columns and filtered topics.

Metadata report
Shows references and metadata such as tags, document state, file location, custom metadata, reference type, file type, and lock status. Users can filter by document state, reference type, file type, missing tags, or specific tags. Metadata can be updated in bulk for selected files: apply or remove tags and change the common next document state. Locked files cannot be selected for metadata updates. Custom metadata columns can be added through Workspace settings > Metadata by specifying a metadata path and display title.

Multimedia report
Shows multimedia used in the map, including multimedia title, location, UUID, media type, used-in references, and reference type. Users can view by multimedia or by used-in references, filter by multimedia type and reference type, refresh, and download an Excel snapshot.

Broken links report
Shows broken links for DITA topics, multimedia, content references, key references, content key references, images, multimedia key references, and related file types. Users can view by broken link or by used-in reference, filter by file type and link type, fix broken links from the report, refresh, and download the filtered snapshot. Fixing a grouped broken link can update all files where the link is used.

title: Overview of document-type shells
content:
Overview of DITA document-type shells

A DITA document-type shell is an XML grammar file that defines which elements and attributes are allowed in a DITA document. It combines structural modules, domain modules, and constraint modules, and also specifies whether and how topics can nest.

How shells fit into configuration
DITA configuration lets organizations define document types that include only the vocabulary modules needed for a specific set of documents. This avoids modifying vocabulary modules directly. Configurations are implemented as document-type shells.

title: DITA metadata
content:
DITA metadata

DITA metadata can be applied in both topics and maps. Topic metadata can be supplemented or overridden by metadata assigned in a DITA map, which supports reuse of the same topic in different maps and usage contexts.

Metadata concepts
Metadata elements, many of which map to Dublin Core metadata, are available in both topics and maps. Metadata attributes support content referencing, conditional processing, application metadata, globalization, and localization. Topic metadata can be specified in a map through topicmeta as well as inside the topic itself. By default, map metadata supplements or overrides topic metadata unless topicmeta lockmeta is set to no.

Cascading and map context
Certain map-level metadata attributes cascade through a containment hierarchy. topicmeta can affect the parent topicref, child topicrefs, and, when directly under map, the map as a whole. Map-to-map references have cascading behavior rules for attributes, metadata elements, and roles. resourceid and ux-window support user-assistance context hooks and window metadata.

title: Metadata elements
content:
DITA metadata elements

DITA metadata elements, many of which map to Dublin Core metadata, are available in topics and maps. This lets authors and information architects use identical metadata markup in both topic-level and map-level contexts.

Where metadata elements appear
The metadata element is a wrapper for many metadata elements. In topics, metadata appears inside prolog. In maps, metadata appears inside topicmeta. In maps, metadata elements can also appear directly in topicmeta. Collections of metadata can be shared between maps and topics using conref or keyref.

Map-level value
Specifying metadata in topicmeta is generally equivalent to specifying it in the prolog of the referenced topic, but the value of map-level metadata is contextual reuse: the same topic can be reused in different maps with different metadata. Many items in topicmeta cascade to nested topicref elements. Not all metadata elements are available inside metadata, but they are available either in topic prolog or map topicmeta.

title: Best practices for content translation
content:
Best practices for content translation in AEM Guides

Before translating DITA content in AEM Guides, folder and file names must follow file naming standards. Avoid spaces, apostrophes, braces, equals signs, special characters, and non-ASCII characters. Language copies should use folders that correspond to the target language, such as de or fr, or language-region folders such as fr-FR or fr-CA. Target locales should match the target language folders configured on the instance.

Folder and configuration rules
The source language folder must have a cloud configuration selected before starting translation. The cloud configuration should be the same as the source folder, and each folder should have only one translation connector configuration. If multiple translation connectors are needed, create multiple folders under /conf. A folder should not contain more than 1000 files.

Permissions and workflow prerequisites
The user who initiates translation needs Read, Modify, Create, and Delete permissions on source and target language folders and must be able to create projects in Adobe Experience Manager. Conditional presets must be created before initiating translation if the map uses them, because the presets are bundled into the translated map version.

Translation workflow rules
Start content translation from the DITA Map console, not from the AEM Assets UI. Do not use the Component-Based DITA Translation Workflow for human translation. Use Component-Based DITA Translation Workflow for machine translation. Globally used content and media that do not require localization should stay outside language copies. Common localized content should be kept in a common folder under the language folder.

Configuring translation service
In Assets UI, select the source language folder, open folder properties, go to the Cloud Services tab, configure the human or machine translation service, and select Save & Close. Only one translation connector configuration should exist in one folder.

Starting the translation job
In Projects console, open the localization project, select the arrow on the Translation Job tile, and select Start. For human translation, export content for translation and import translated content back into the translation project. Translation status can be viewed from the ellipsis on the Translation Job tile. When complete, status changes to Ready to Review, and the user accepts the translated copy and asset metadata from the Translation Job tile.

Rejection and cancellation behavior
If translation is rejected for one or more topics, rejected topics revert from In Progress to their original status, based on the latest translation state. Translation files already created in the destination language folder are not deleted. If a topic belongs to multiple projects and one project rejects, deletes, or cancels the job, the topic's In Progress status does not revert globally; only that project is removed from the asset's In Progress project list. Canceling/deleting the translation job or deleting the entire project reverts In Progress status to the original status.

title: Translate documents from the Map Console
content:
Translate documents from the Map Console in AEM Guides

For AEM Guides as a Cloud Service February 2022 or later, Adobe recommends using the Editor translation feature. The Map Console Translation tab lets users create new translation projects, add jobs to existing translation projects, or create multi-lingual translation projects for all selected target languages. Administrators can configure the Manage tab used for translation in the Editor.

Before starting
Create a root folder for source content using the language name or language code such as English or en. Create destination language folders such as de or fr at the same level as the source folder. Only target folders parallel to the source folder are selectable; missing target folders or target language equal to source appear grayed out with a warning. If target folders are created after language groups, refresh the browser.

Create a translation project
Open a DITA map in Repository panel Map View, select Open in map console, go to Translation tab, select language groups or individual languages, choose version scope, then Apply. Version scope options are None for default versions, Use Baseline for files in a selected baseline, or Use Latest Version as on to filter files by creation date/time. The topic/assets table supports filters for Title, File Name, File Type, Reference Type, Version, Version Label, Target Version, Document State, Target Language, Translation Status, and Target Label. Translation Status values include Out of Sync, Missing Copy, In Progress, and In Sync.

Sending for translation
Select topics/assets, choose Send for Translation, then create a new translation project, create structure only, create a new XLIFF translation project, create a multi-lingual translation project, add to an existing project, or create a scoping translation project. XLIFF uses version 1.2 and only works with human translation configuration. A multi-lingual project creates translation jobs for all selected languages. Adding to an existing project updates draft job entries when possible; otherwise it creates a new job or project depending on destination language and job status. A scoping project does not send copies for translation and maintains original translation status.

Reference and asset behavior
When translating maps with DITAVAL and Markdown references based on the working copy, images and linked assets are included when they exist in the source language folder. These references appear in the Translation Dashboard reference list and can be explicitly selected for translation. During translation, referenced assets are copied into the target language folder and handled consistently with image translation behavior.

Translation rules and SRX
Administrators can configure translation rules using SRX files. SRX files should be named with language codes such as en-US or ar-AE; names are not case-sensitive and hyphen/underscore are both resolved. SRX files can be placed under content/dam, and the folder path is configured in Translation SRX location in the folder profile. AEM Guides picks SRX rules based on the source language and falls back to out-of-the-box rules when no custom SRX exists.

Version labels and differences
An administrator can enable Propagate source version labels to the target version under Workspace settings > Translation. Source labels such as Release 1.0 can then be applied to target copies. The source label is attached to one target version; moving the source label updates the latest target label. For Out of Sync DITA files, users can select Show difference to compare the last translated version and selected version.

Out-of-sync and in-progress handling
Minor Out of Sync changes can be dismissed by selecting out-of-sync assets, choosing Mark In Sync, and confirming Force Sync. Mark In Sync appears only for Out of Sync assets. In Progress links open an In Progress Projects dialog listing translation projects and target languages containing the selected reference. This in-progress project view is available for Cloud Service February 2023 or later.

Project cleanup
For new translation projects created in AEM Guides 2404 or later, administrators can configure Translation project cleanup after completion in Workspace settings > Translation to delete or disable completed translation projects. Deleting removes project files/folders. Disabling keeps the project in the repository but prevents update/edit. Cleanup does not affect translation status of references.

content:
AEM Guides reports suite decision guide

Use this consolidated learned chunk when the user asks which AEM Guides report to use, how reports differ, or how to explain report behavior with confidence.

Choose the right report
Use Map Console Reports when the user is working on one current DITA map and needs operational map cleanup: topic list, metadata, multimedia usage, or broken links. Use the Map Dashboard DITA Map Report when the user needs an administrator-style integrity view for a map before publishing: missing topics, missing elements, UUIDs, review status, Used In references, and downloadable CSV. Use Content Reuse Report when the user asks about reuse metrics, most reused topic, Number of Times Reused, Referenced By, or average content reuse. Use Conversion Status Report when the question is about source-document conversion tasks such as Word, structured HTML, XML, DocBook, or IDML conversions and their Success/Failed/Active/Queued status. Use Reverted files version history when the question is about audit history for files reverted to earlier versions, including Revert From, Revert To, user, timestamp, and comment.

Operational access patterns
Map Console Reports are opened from a DITA map in Map View by selecting Open in map console and then Reports. Map Dashboard report is opened from Assets UI by selecting the DITA map and choosing Reports. Content Reuse Report is opened from Tools > Guides > Content Reuse Report. Conversion Status Report is opened from Tools > Guides > Conversion Status Report. Reverted version history is opened from Assets UI Version History > Revert Version Logs, topic preview Version History, or Tools > Guides > Version Revert History.

Answering confidence rules
Do not treat all reports as interchangeable. If the user says broken links, metadata bulk update, topic list, multimedia, or current map cleanup, answer from Map Console Reports. If the user says missing topics, missing elements, review status, UUIDs, Used In, Generate Report, CSV, or administrator pre-publish integrity check, answer from Map Dashboard report. If the user says reuse count, average reuse, content reuse instances, referenced by, or most reused topic, answer from Content Reuse Report. If the user says conversion logs, Word, DocBook, IDML, or conversion status, answer from Conversion Status Report. If the user says revert, previous version, version history, Revert From, or audit trail, answer from Reverted files version history.

Common pitfalls
Content Reuse Report requires post-processing workflows. Content Reuse counts first-level direct content references and topic references, and Number of Times Reused equals Referenced By entries minus one. Map Console Metadata report cannot update locked files. Conversion Status Date Added downloads the conversion log. Reverted files version history can cover one file or all files in a folder.

title: Add translation rules with SRX files
content:
Add translation rules with SRX files in AEM Guides

AEM Guides lets administrators configure translation segmentation rules by using SRX files. SRX stands for Segmentation Rules eXchange, a standard format for exchanging segmentation rules across users and translation environments.

How to name SRX files
SRX files should be named with the language code, such as en-US.srx or ar-AE.srx. The title/case of the language code is not case-sensitive, so en-US, en-us, or EN-us can resolve. AEM Guides can also resolve hyphen and underscore separators, so en-US and en_US are treated as acceptable forms.

Where to store SRX files
Create a folder containing the custom SRX files. The folder can be placed anywhere under the Adobe Experience Manager assets root, which is ./content/dam. For better performance, the configured folder should contain only SRX files.

How AEM Guides picks rules
After creating the folder, add the folder path in the Translation SRX location configuration inside the folder profile. AEM Guides picks SRX rules according to the source language of the translation project. If a custom SRX file for that source language is not defined, AEM Guides uses the out-of-the-box translation rules.

content:
Translate modified topics in AEM Guides

When source topics change after translation, those topics can require re-translation. AEM Guides lets users track modified topics from the DITA map in the source language copy folder through the Map Console Translation tab.

How Out of Sync is detected
Open the source language DITA map in Map Console, select the Translation tab, choose available languages in the Translation panel, and select Apply. AEM Guides shows translation status for each topic. Topics whose source has another revision than the revision sent for translation appear as Out of Sync. The translation workflow compares the last saved revision of the source language topic file with the translated version.

Re-translation workflow
Select the Out of Sync topics, then choose Send for Translation. Users can create a new translation project or add the topics to an existing translation project, provide the required project details, and select Submit. A confirmation message shows the topic has been sent for translation. In Project console, a translation job card is created. Use the ellipsis to view assets in the job folder. Select the arrow on the translation job card and choose Start to begin translation. The job status can also be viewed from the ellipsis at the bottom of the job card.

Mark in Sync override
When an Out of Sync topic is selected, the Mark in Sync button appears above the title bar. Use Mark in Sync only when the source changes are minor and do not require translation. Selecting Mark in Sync sets the selected Out of Sync topic status to In Sync.

Human translation behavior
If using human translation, export content for translation and import translated content back into the translation project.

Review and DAM copy behavior
After translation completes, status changes to Ready to Review. Use the ellipsis to view topic details. Select Reveal in Assets to view and verify the translation, Accept Translation if translated correctly, or Reject Translation if the job must be redone. Accept or Reject is required; otherwise the file remains in a temporary location and is not copied to DAM. After accepted re-translation, returning to the source language DITA map in Assets UI shows the re-translated topics as In Sync.

title: Use condition presets
content:
Use condition presets in AEM Guides

Condition presets define what happens to profiled DITA content in final output. Authors add conditional attributes and values in DITA topics, such as version 1.0 vs 2.0 or platform Windows vs Linux. A condition preset then includes, excludes, passes through, or flags matching content during output generation.

Where condition presets are created
AEM Guides supports creating and managing condition presets from both Map console and Map dashboard. In Map console, condition presets are available from the left panel and can be used in Output presets. In Map dashboard, they are available from the Condition Presets tab.

Create condition preset from Map console
Open the DITA map in Map console, navigate to Condition presets, select the plus icon, enter a unique preset name, and select Create. Empty names, invalid characters, or duplicate names show errors. Hyphen and underscore are valid separators. Select the preset to view attributes and actions. The Attributes panel shows all attributes added to references in the map. Users can add whole attributes, selected attribute values, dragged attribute/value pairs, or Select all. Default action for added attributes is Include. Select Add to move attributes to the right panel. Use Remove to remove selected attributes. Optionally override actions with Include, Exclude, Passthrough, or Flag. Select Save. Closing or switching presets without saving shows a warning. Saved condition presets appear in the Condition presets dropdown of Output presets.

Manage condition preset from Map console
Hover over a preset and use Options to Rename, Duplicate, or Delete. Duplicate defaults to selected condition preset name plus _1, but the name can be changed.

Create condition preset from Map dashboard
Select the Condition Presets tab in the DITA map dashboard, select Create, enter the name in Name Condition, and choose a default action from Include, Exclude, Passthrough, or Flag. The default action applies to all condition attributes, including attributes not explicitly added to the preset. Add individual attributes with Add or all attributes with Add all. Optionally override the default action for selected conditions by choosing an action and selecting Apply, or by using the Action dropdown for an attribute. Select Save.

Manage condition preset from Map dashboard
Use Edit to change actions in an existing condition preset. Use Duplicate to create a copy; the default duplicate name is selected condition preset name plus _Duplicate. Use Remove to delete selected condition presets and confirm with Remove.

title: Conditional attribute profiling
content:
Conditional attribute profiling in AEM Guides

Conditional attributes are standardized tags that authors apply to DITA topics, maps, or repository assets so publishers can include, exclude, pass through, or flag content during output generation. Example uses include platform-specific content such as Windows, Mac, Unix, or Linux.

Scope and visibility
AEM Guides supports conditional attributes defined globally or at a folder level. Globally defined conditions are visible across all projects. Folder-specific conditions are visible only in projects created within that folder. Authors can then use those attributes to conditionalize content, and publishers can use condition presets to decide which conditions are included or excluded in the output.

Permissions and profile limitations
Users can create or edit conditional attributes only in a Folder Profile they can access. If an administrator has not granted Folder Profile access, the user cannot create or edit conditional attributes there. The global profile cannot be edited.

How to define conditional attributes
Go to Tools > Guides > Folder Profiles, select a Folder Profile, open the Conditional Attributes tab, and select Edit. Select Add, then enter Name, Value, and Label for the attribute. A profile can be saved with only the attribute name, but the attribute becomes usable only after a value is specified. If both value and label are specified, the Editor shows only the value to authors; the label is shown to the publishing administrator when creating a condition preset. Use the plus icon to add additional values/labels for the same attribute. Use Add again to add more attributes, then Save.

Authoring behavior
After saving, the conditional attribute is stored in the system. When authors work on DITA topics in the relevant folder, they can view and apply the conditional attribute values from the Properties tab in the Editor.

title: Create and manage baselines from Map console
content:
Create and manage baselines from Map console in AEM Guides

A baseline is a saved version set of topics and assets that can be used for publishing or translation. A single DITA map can have multiple baselines, but each output preset in a DITA map can be associated with only one baseline. If no baseline is selected for publishing, AEM Guides publishes the latest content version. Selecting a baseline for translation is optional, but translated baseline contents are saved with translated copies and can later be shared externally or archived.

Baseline creation
Open the DITA map in Map console, go to the Baseline tab, and select the plus icon. In New baseline, enter Name, choose Configuration as Manual update or Automatic update, and select Apply. Baseline creation is asynchronous; users can continue working and receive a pop-up plus Inbox notification when it completes.

Manual update baseline
Manual update creates a static baseline using topic/reference versions based on a date/time or label. Date selects topic versions as of a specified date and time. Label selects topic versions with the chosen label. Label loading is batched in groups of 20 with infinite scrolling and case-insensitive alphabetical order. If a label does not exist and the user chooses not to create a baseline, creation fails and shows an error near the baseline name. For direct references, users can use latest versions for topics without the selected label. For indirect references, users can also Pick Automatically so referenced content versions match the version of the content where they are referenced. Topic and media selections are saved in the backend and are not shown in the UI.

Automatic update baseline
Automatic update creates a dynamic baseline based on labels. Dynamic baselines are updated when labels move to newer versions. If a baseline is generated, downloaded, or used for translation, files are picked dynamically based on current label assignments. Labels selected earlier have higher priority. For indirect references, options include Pick automatically, Use selected label, or Use latest version / working copy.

Managing baselines
The Baseline panel supports search, filtering by creation status Successful/In-Progress/Failed, refresh, and selecting a baseline to view/edit. Static baseline editing is recommended only for a small number of reference changes; changing the main DITA map version can force reference recalculation and fail on large maps. For large maps, create a new baseline or edit baseline properties. Dynamic baseline editing changes properties because references are generated at runtime from labels.

Existing baseline actions
Options menu actions include Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Manage labels, Edit properties, and Export Baseline. Duplicate can create an exact copy or duplicate based on a selected label. Default duplicate name is selected baseline name plus suffix, such as sample-baseline_1. Manage labels is asynchronous and sends notification after labels are added or removed. Export Baseline exports a Microsoft Excel snapshot with details such as title, file name, file type, version number, and document state.

Baseline filters and saving
Baseline Filters can filter by file name, file location, File Type, Reference Type, and other columns; users can choose columns and sort by column headings. After editing a baseline, select Save to keep changes or Reset to discard them. Reset warns that unsaved changes will be lost.

title: Work with Baseline from the Map dashboard
content:
Work with Baseline from the Map dashboard in AEM Guides

The Map dashboard Baselines tab lets users create baselines and use them for publishing or translation. A baseline records selected versions of topics and referenced content so that every time the baseline is used in output generation or translation, those exact selected versions are included. Multiple output presets of the same DITA map can be published in parallel.

Create a baseline
Open a DITA map in the Assets UI, go to the Baselines page, select Create, enter Baseline Name, then choose how versions are selected. Label selects topics and assets that have the chosen label. Version on selects topic and asset versions as of a specified date and time, using the Adobe Experience Manager server timezone rather than the user's local timezone. After selecting the label or date/time, referenced topics and media are selected and stored in the backend; this full selection is not shown in the UI.

Label behavior
When creating by Label, users can optionally use the latest version for topics or media files that do not have the specified label. If this option is not selected and any topic or media file lacks the label, baseline creation fails. Creating a baseline by labels applies Pick Automatically to all referenced content versions.

View baseline contents
Selecting a baseline in the Baselines tab shows the DITA map file, map contents or topics, and referenced content. Columns include Name, Kind, Version, Version Date and Time, Latest, Parent Map, Label, and Referenced By. Sub-map referenced topics are displayed in the Content section, while referenced assets show the parent topic in Referenced By.

Edit baseline contents
To edit a baseline, select the baseline and choose Edit. Users can rename it or manually change selected topic and referenced content versions. Browse Topic lets users choose a topic and select a version. Browse All Topics loads all topics and media referred from the DITA map, but can take time for large nested maps. Referenced content can use Pick Automatically so the system selects the version that corresponds to the content version where the reference was made. If referenced files are not versioned, baseline creation creates a version for them when auto-create version is enabled; this is also required for translation.

Duplicate, remove, and label baselines
Duplicate creates a copy of an existing baseline with a different name and selected topic/reference versions. Remove deletes a baseline. Add Labels applies one label to multiple topics and referenced content in a baseline. A baseline cannot receive labels for latest-version items because labels can be added only to versioned topics or assets. If configured, predefined labels appear in a drop-down. Users can also apply labels to child maps and their dependents.

Export translated baseline
A baseline can be used during translation by selecting Use Baseline in the Translation tab. Exporting a translated baseline is possible only after the content in that baseline has been translated. A baseline version that has not been translated cannot be exported. If a translated baseline was already exported, users can choose Overwrite Existing Baseline and export again.

title: New baseline Beta in Experience Manager Guides
content:
New baseline Beta in Experience Manager Guides

Scope and availability
The new baseline feature is a Beta capability available with Experience Manager Guides 2026.04.0. It provides a redesigned baseline architecture for better performance, stability, and consistency on large, complex maps. Customers must contact the Customer Success Team to enable it. The new baseline model uses the same Map console workflows as the existing baseline feature, but it does not support creating or managing baselines from Map dashboard.

Why it exists
The new baseline model addresses slow loading, poor responsiveness for large baselines, inconsistent baseline states caused by partial updates or failed validations, limited visibility and control for extensive baseline content, and performance bottlenecks during baseline creation, updates, or rebuilds.

Key enhancements
The model uses incremental loading and a streamlined data structure for scalability. UI changes appear only after successful backend validation, preventing invalid baseline states. Filtering, sorting, navigation, pagination, document state filtering, label filtering, file type filtering, reference type filtering, GUID-based search, and filtering files with no labels are supported. Dependency impact is previewed before version changes are applied. Labels can be moved between versions within a baseline. Editing uses row-level updates and loads expensive data such as version trees and dependency differences only during version updates. Save operations are deterministic. Baseline creation uses stored reference data rather than runtime parsing and validates required version information upfront. REST APIs and the Java SDK support the new baseline model.

Behavior changes before migration
Direct map references are classified as DIRECT. Invalid references are skipped. Reltable references remain excluded. Pick Automatically is evaluated immediately before resolving direct references. Version 1.0 is mandatory, and baselines with missing or ambiguous versions can resolve differently after migration. During migration, DIRECT references take precedence, unpinned references move to latest version, and metadata is added from version 5.0 onward. The new graph-based baseline model removes mutable fields and is not backward compatible with the previous baseline model. Raw baseline objects are no longer exposed. After migration, version purging considers only baselines stored in the new baseline repository.

Migration process
After Customer Success enables the feature, migrate existing baselines through Tools > Guides > Bulk Processor. Start a New Process, set Feature type to Baseline, select folders and files to process, optionally select folders to ignore, and select Create. A success popup confirms the asset processing task was triggered. Users can view processing status and select View logs to download migration logs. Logs include counts such as maps migrated and baselines successfully migrated. No baseline edits should be made during migration, especially in working copies. After migration, some baselines may require rebuilding if versions are missing.

Using the new baseline
The new model keeps common Map console baseline workflows unless noted. Export baseline is renamed to Download for baselines created with both Manual and Automatic updates. Dynamic baselines can be opened from the Baseline panel and managed from the Options menu. Dynamic baseline actions include Edit properties and Rebuild. Download supports pagination and includes all baseline content matching applied filters, not only currently visible rows.

Editing references
To edit a new baseline reference, open the baseline from the Baseline panel, use the tabular reference view, hover over the target file, select the Edit icon, choose the required version from the Version dropdown, review the preview of added and removed dependencies, and select Update. If no dependency changes are detected, an empty-state message is shown. The selected version then updates the baseline.

title: New Baseline migration FAQ
content:
New Baseline migration FAQ in AEM Guides

Purpose
This FAQ answers common questions about New Baseline migration, behavior changes, migration considerations, and expected outcomes when upgrading to the New Baseline model.

Benefits
Migrating to the New Baseline model provides improved performance and scalability, better UI and backend consistency, deterministic editing and saving, enhanced filtering and navigation, dependency impact previews, improved reliability during baseline creation and updates, and better API and automation support.

Migration scope and version behavior
Migration creates new baselines only for the current working copy of a map. Baselines associated with other working copies are not included in that migration. If a user restores or accesses a previous version of a map, baselines associated with that version are automatically migrated to the new baseline model through an asynchronous migration process.

Reference handling
Invalid references are skipped during migration to preserve consistency and reliability. Migration retains all valid baseline content and references exactly as they are. Apart from removing invalid references, migration does not change references or dependency resolution behavior until the migrated baseline is modified, rebuilt, or newly created with the new baseline model. Reltable references are excluded from baseline resolution, matching legacy behavior. Direct map references are classified as DIRECT, given highest precedence, and resolved before other reference types. References with scope="peer" are not included in the baseline model to improve publishing performance and avoid unnecessary dependency resolution.

Map Dashboard support
New Baseline supports baseline management only from the Map Console. Creating and managing baselines from the Map Dashboard is not supported.

Migration precautions and missing versions
Do not modify baselines while migration is in progress, especially in working copies. Changes during migration can cause failures or inconsistent baseline states. Some baselines might need to be rebuilt after migration if referenced versions are no longer available or accessible.

Approximate On-Premise migration time
Migration time depends on the number of baselines, total references, repository size and complexity, hardware configuration, and available system resources. Based on internal observations for repositories with about 18,000 references, a single baseline can take a few seconds, 10 to 15 baselines can take a few tens of seconds, and 25 to 50 baselines can take about 1 to 2 minutes. These are reference figures only and can vary by environment.

Rollback behavior
Rollback to Old Baselines is possible. When rollback is performed, old baselines are restored to their state at migration time. Changes made while old baseline configuration was disabled and new baseline configuration was active are not reflected in restored old baselines. Original old baseline objects remain at their original location, and disabling the new baseline configuration switches the system back to those original objects.

Prerequisites and backup
Migration can be performed when minimum version requirements are met: AEM Guides On-Premise version 5.2 or later, or AEM Guides Cloud Service release 2026.05.0 or later. No additional backup is required specifically for New Baseline migration. However, working-copy baselines can be lost if a user later reverts to an earlier map version; if preserving those baselines matters, back them up before migration.

title: Manage Global and Folder Profile output presets
content:
Manage Global and Folder Profile output presets in AEM Guides

Scope and permissions
Global and Folder Profile output presets are available only to folder-level administrative users. Administrators can create and manage presets at the Global or Folder Profile level so the presets can be reused to generate output for all maps related to that profile.

Create a profile-level output preset
Select the DITA map for which the output preset is needed. From the map file Options menu, select Edit Topics to open the map in the Editor. Select the Open in map console icon. In Map console, open the Output presets tab and select the plus icon to create a preset for the DITA map. In the Add preset dialog, enter Type, Name, and Target when creating a Knowledgebase preset. Select Add to folder profile to create the preset for the related folder profile, then select Add. The preset appears under the Output presets tab for all related maps, and a folder-profile icon identifies it as a folder profile level preset.

Configuration behavior
After creating the preset, enter its configuration details. Folder Profile presets are independent of individual maps, so map-specific configurations are not available for those presets. AEM Guides also provides an out-of-box PDF output preset for DITA maps.

Generate and inspect output
Users can select the Generate output icon at the top-right to generate output for maps related to the created output preset. They can view the output generation status and select View Output in the Success dialog to inspect the generated output.

Options menu operations
From the preset Options menu, users can Generate output for an existing preset, use View output and View log quick links, Rename an output preset, Duplicate it, Delete it, or choose Default PDF to make an existing PDF preset the default preset used by Download as PDF for a map. If a Global or Folder Profile output preset is deleted, the deletion is reflected in all related maps and the preset no longer appears under their Output presets tab.

title: Use variables for output destination and file options
content:
Use variables for output destination and file options in AEM Guides

Purpose
When generating AEM Sites or PDF output, users can use variables to define Destination Path, Site path, AEM Site Name, or PDF File Name. A single variable or a combination of variables can be used.

Supported out-of-box variables
${map_filename} uses the DITA map file name. For example, a destination path such as /content/output/sites/${map_filename} can resolve under a folder based on the DITA map name.

${map_title} uses the DITA map title. For example, /content/output/sites/${map_title} uses the map title in the output path.

${preset_name} uses the output preset name. For example, /content/output/sites/${preset_name} can create output under a folder named after the selected preset.

${language_code} uses the language code where the map file is located. For a map path under /content/dam/projects/AEM-Guides/en/user-guide/, ${language_code} resolves to en.

${map_parentpath} uses the complete path of the map file to create the destination path. This variable cannot be used to specify AEM Site Name or PDF File Name.

${path_after_langfolder} uses the part of the map path after the language folder. For a map under /content/dam/projects/AEM-Guides/en/user-guide/, it resolves to user-guide. This variable cannot be used to specify AEM Site Name or PDF File Name.

${system_date} uses the current server date. ${system_time} uses the current server time. These are useful when output locations need date or time based separation.

Metadata as variables
Metadata defined on the DITA map or bookmap under /jcr:content/metadata can also be used as variables. For example, if dc:title is defined under the metadata node, ${dc:title} uses that title value in the final output.

title: Pass metadata to output using DITA-OT
content:
Pass metadata to output using DITA-OT in AEM Guides

Purpose
Metadata is additional information about the output. In AEM Guides, users can pass existing metadata or custom metadata tags to AEM, PDF, HTML5, EPUB, and Custom format outputs when using DITA-OT publishing.

Using Map console
Open the DITA map in Map console. Select and open the output preset where metadata should be passed, such as a PDF preset. Ensure the preset is created using the DITA-OT option. From the File properties dropdown, select the metadata fields to pass to DITA-OT publishing. The dropdown lists both default and custom properties. Selected properties appear below the dropdown. Select Save, then Generate output. The selected metadata properties are passed to the DITA-OT generated output.

Using Map dashboard
In Assets UI, navigate to the DITA map. Select and edit the output preset where metadata should be passed, such as a PDF preset. Select the DITA-OT option in that preset. From the Properties dropdown, select the required custom and default metadata fields, such as author, dc:title, and dc:description. Selected properties appear below the dropdown. Select Done to save changes, then generate output. The selected metadata properties are passed to the DITA-OT generated output.

Default metadata properties and overlay
The default metadata properties are dc:description, dc:language, dc:title, and docstate. These are picked from the metadataList file at /libs/fmdita/config/metadataList. Administrators can overlay this file at /apps/fmdita/config/metadataList to control available metadata fields. Custom properties can also be passed when values are already defined.

Deprecation note
As of the 2502 release of Experience Manager Guides, passing root map metadata arguments through the DITA-OT command line is deprecated. To avoid disruption, a Config.Manager property is available to enable or disable that functionality through output generation settings.

title: Use Map Collection for output generation
content:
Use Map Collection for output generation in AEM Guides

Purpose
A Map Collection lets publishing specialists organize multiple DITA maps and generate output for multiple documents in a single batch. Each map in the collection can have different output presets enabled or disabled. The collection dashboard also shows whether a map has changed since its last generated output so users can decide whether to republish.

Create a Map Collection and add DITA maps
Open the Experience Manager Guides Home page and select Map collections. Users can also open Assets UI and select Map Collections; if unavailable, use Navigation in the left rail and then Map Collections. On the Map Collections page, select Create, provide a Collection Title, and select Create. Open the new collection by selecting its tile. In the map collection dashboard, select Edit, then Add Maps, locate and add the required DITA maps. By default, all presets and locales associated with each map are added automatically. Turn the desired output sliding buttons on or off, then select Done.

Filters and map details
The collection page left rail provides filters for Modified, Preset, and Language. Modified can show only maps changed since last publication. Preset filters maps by configured output preset, such as AEM Site. Language filters by language code. The Maps and Presets table shows Map, Filename, Language, Preset, Baseline, Modified, and Last Generated. Baseline shows the baseline used by the output preset, or a hyphen if none is used.

Configure and generate output
Open the Map Collection to view AEM Sites, PDF including Native PDF, HTML5, EPUB, Custom presets, and administrator-created global or folder profile presets. A folder profile icon marks folder-profile presets. Users can apply filters or enter Edit mode to enable or disable desired outputs. New presets are disabled by default. Presets can be enabled individually, through Enable All presets for a DITA map, or through Enable Folder profile presets for a DITA map. To generate output for selected maps, select the map files and choose Generate Selected. To generate output for all DITA maps with configured presets, choose Generate All. If output generation for a preset or DITA map is queued or in progress, another output generation task cannot be started for the same preset or map.

Bulk metadata configuration
Within a Map Collection, users can select Configure Metadata to open the Asset Metadata page and update metadata properties in bulk for maps in the collection. All maps are selected by default, but users can choose specific maps. They can view and update properties such as metadata, schedule activation or deactivation, references, document state, and more. Select Save & Close to save updates, Append to append new tags to existing tag lists, or Submit from the Save & Close dropdown. Document State choices are limited to states allowed in common for all selected maps. Updated metadata stays in sync with file properties and is visible in the File Properties panel in the Editor.

Delete and cancel
To delete a map collection, select it on the Map Collections page and choose Delete. To remove a DITA map from a collection, open the collection in Edit mode, select the map file, and choose Remove From Collection; this also removes associated presets and locales from that collection. To cancel a publish job, open the Outputs tab of the Map Collection, find the task, and select the Cancel This Job icon.

title: Use New map collection for output generation
content:
Use New map collection for output generation in AEM Guides

Availability and purpose
New map collection is a Beta feature available in Experience Manager Guides as a Cloud Service starting with the 2026.06.0 release. Customers must contact their Customer Success team to enable it. The New map collection consolidates capabilities that were previously spread across old map collection and bulk publishing into one unified interface for maps, presets, generation history, publishing history, metadata, and collection membership.

Create a New map collection and add maps
Open the Experience Manager Guides Home page and select New map collections. On the Map collections page, select Create, provide a Name, and select Create. Open the desired collection, select Edit collection, then Add maps. Select maps and optionally enable Select available translations to automatically add all available translation copies of each map; if no translations exist, the default language is added. Select Add. Select required maps or all listed maps, then choose Fetch presets to retrieve available presets.

Preset grouping and filtering
Fetched presets are grouped into Folder profile presets and Other presets. Folder profile presets are common to all selected maps. Other presets are specific to individual maps, and the associated map is indicated next to each preset toggle. Users can choose Enable all presets or Enable all folder profile presets. A Filter icon supports two-level filtering: Preset types to narrow listed presets and Map status to choose specific maps from the Maps panel. Select Save to store selected maps and presets.

Maps and Presets tab
The Maps and Presets tab shows selected maps for a specific language with columns for Preset, Baseline, Modified since generation, Modified since published, Last generated, and Last published. Baseline shows the baseline used by the output preset, or a hyphen if none is used. Modified since generation and Modified since published help users decide whether generation or republishing is needed.

Filters
The right panel provides filters for Modified since generation, Modified since publishing, Presets, and Language. Modified filters support Yes, No, or Not yet generated. Preset filters display maps configured with the selected output preset. Language filters display selected language codes.

Generate output
Open the Map Collection, select the required maps and specific presets, then select Generate. Users cannot start another output generation task for the same preset or DITA map while a task for that preset or map is queued or in progress. Generated history lists generated maps and shows progress in the Status column. Status values include Finished in green for success, Finished in red for completed with errors, and Executing in blue for in-progress generation. Users can Refresh status, cancel an executing task with the Cancel generation icon, open generated output with the Open Output icon, or view logs with the Logs icon.

Publish output
If publishing is configured, select maps from either Maps and Presets or Generated history, then choose Publish to. Select the target environment, either Preview or Publish instance. Use the Published history tab to monitor publishing status, Refresh to update status, and verify published content after status becomes Successful.

Configure metadata
From the Maps and presets tab, select Configure Metadata to open the Asset Metadata page. All maps in the collection are selected by default, but users can choose specific maps. Users can update metadata, schedule activation or deactivation, references, document state, and more. Select Save & Close, optionally Append tags from the Save & Close dropdown, and Submit. Document State choices are limited to states allowed in common for all selected maps. Updated metadata stays synchronized with file properties and is visible in the Editor File Properties panel.

title: AEM Guides test-plan Claude skill package setup
content:
AEM Guides test-plan Claude skill package setup

Team members do not need to clone the full repository. The central VM hosts the backend, MCP gateway, Jira/RAG retrieval, enriched AEM Guides behavior chunks, DITA/DITA-OT indexes, and repository evidence. Team members only install the small Claude skill package locally and configure Claude Code MCP to point at the VM backend.

Download/package artifact in the repository: release-artifacts/aem-guides-test-plan-claude-skill.zip

The ZIP contains: skills/aem-guides-test-scenario-generator/, commands/guides-test-plan-generator.md, install.ps1, install.sh, README.md, and manifest.json.

Install on Windows: extract the ZIP and run install.ps1, or copy skills/aem-guides-test-scenario-generator/ to %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\aem-guides-test-scenario-generator\ and commands/guides-test-plan-generator.md to %USERPROFILE%\.claude\commands\guides-test-plan-generator.md.

Install on macOS/Linux: extract the ZIP and run ./install.sh, or copy skills/aem-guides-test-scenario-generator/ to ~/.claude/skills/aem-guides-test-scenario-generator/ and commands/guides-test-plan-generator.md to ~/.claude/commands/guides-test-plan-generator.md.

After installation, restart Claude Code and run /guides-test-plan-generator GUIDES-12345. The slash command requires the MCP tool guides_test_plan_generator. The local skill supplies workflow and quality gates; evidence comes from the VM RAG/MCP backend.
